rows.figure: 39,000 · about 3.56 per 100,000 (GHE 2019 release, as printed by WHO AFRO)
rows.scope: Drowning deaths in the WHO African Region in 2019 as estimated in the WHO Global Health Estimates 2019 release (legacy vintage, the one behind who-ghe-2019). Printed rounded ('an estimated 39 000'); the rate is printed as 'about 3.56' per 100 000 in the Figure 1 text and 3.6 in the Deaths section. The fact sheet names no ICD codes.
rows.source: WHO Regional Office for Africa, integrated African Health Observatory (iAHO), Analytical Fact Sheet 'Drowning... a leading cause of unintentional injury death', July 2023; data source stated as WHO Global Health Estimates 2019
rows.do_not_add_to: A different model vintage from who-region-afr (GHE 2021 release: 66,000 in 2021). WHO states revision series are not comparable, so never set 39,000 (2019) beside 66,000 (2021) as a trend. A share of who-ghe-2019 only; never added to who-ghe-2021 or to any GHE 2023 figure.
rows.note: Shows how large the revision between GHE releases is for Africa (39,000 in the 2019 release versus 66,000 in the 2021 release); the gap is mostly re-estimation, not a rise. The fact sheet also says the Region's crude rate fell 'from 5.1 to 3.6' per 100 000 between 2000 and 2019 and puts the Western Pacific Region at 3.8 per 100 000 in 2019. Not the unrounded figure the task asked for.

rows.figure: 70,000 (GHE 2019 release, as printed by WHO SEARO)
rows.scope: Drowning deaths in the WHO South-East Asia Region in 2019, from the WHO Global Health Estimates 2019 release (the release linked from the news item). Printed rounded ('an estimated 70 000'); no rate printed. Cause definition not stated on the page.
rows.source: WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia, news release 'Nearly two thirds of global drowning deaths occur in Asia Pacific', 22 July 2021 (launch of the regional status reports on drowning in South-East Asia and the Western Pacific)
rows.do_not_add_to: A different model vintage from who-region-sear (GHE 2021 release: 83,000 in 2021); never read the two as a 2019-to-2021 change. A share of who-ghe-2019 only. The release's combined 'over 144 000' for Asia Pacific is its own printed total, not ours.
rows.note: The same release gives 74 000 for the Western Pacific Region (row who-ghe2019-region-wpr) and says the two regions held 61% of global drowning deaths in 2019. The regional status reports themselves (WHO IRIS handles 10665/343085 and 10665/343073) were not opened; they may print the unrounded 2019 figure.

rows.figure: 74,000 (GHE 2019 release, as printed by WHO SEARO and WPRO)
rows.scope: Drowning deaths in the WHO Western Pacific Region in 2019, from the WHO Global Health Estimates 2019 release. Printed rounded ('an estimated ... 74 000'); the WPRO data page prints the same 74 000 against 120 000 in 2000. No rate printed on either page; WHO AFRO's July 2023 fact sheet gives the Region 3.8 per 100 000 in 2019. Cause definition not stated.
rows.source: WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia, news release of 22 July 2021 (joint launch with WHO WPRO); same figure on the WHO Western Pacific Health Data Platform page 'World Drowning Prevention Day 2023'
rows.do_not_add_to: A different model vintage from who-region-wpr (GHE 2021 release: 84,000 in 2021); never read as a trend against it. A share of who-ghe-2019 only. The 2000 figure (120 000) is a back-cast from the same model.
rows.note: WPRO page: https://data.wpro.who.int/world-drowning-prevention-day-2023/ ('from 120 000 to 74 000 deaths per year'). notes: Result: the unrounded regional drowning deaths and rates for 2019, 2021 and 2023 were NOT found in any HTML, JSON or PDF source; they exist only in Excel workbooks that the fetch tool returns as '[binary data]'. No figure here is summed or computed by us. What a person with a browser should do: (1) Download https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/gho-documents/global-health-estimates/deaths_whoregion_2026-09-30.xlsx?sfvrsn=b1e96052_1 ('WHO regions' link on https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/themes/mortality-and-global-health-estimates/ghe-leading-causes-of-death, described as 'Summary tables of mortality estimates by cause, age and sex, globally and by region, 2000-2023'). The page states no sheet names. Look for the GHE cause row labelled 'Drowning' (expected under Injuries, Unintentional injuries; the ICD-10 codes WHO uses for its drowning estimates are W65-W74 per the 2024 report, p. 8), both sexes, all ages, for each of the six regions and for the years 2019, 2021 and 2023; record sheet name, row label and the exact cell values and whether deaths are in thousands. The global companion is deaths_global_2026-09-30.xlsx?sfvrsn=22004518_1 and the income-group file deaths_wbincome_2026-09-30.xlsx?sfvrsn=476c620d_1. Country-level files for 2019, 2021 and 2023 (deaths_bycountry_age_sex_<year>_2026-10-01.xlsx) also exist, and rate files age-standardized-death-rates-2000-2023_bycountry_2026-10-01.xlsx and crude-death-rates-2000-2023_bycountry_2026-10-01.xlsx (country level only; the page lists no regional rate file, so a regional rate may have to be read from the deaths file if it carries one, or is not published). (2) Important vintage caveat for the acceptance check 'do the 2021 values match the report's rounded figures': the page now serves the GHE 2023 release (recommended citation 'Global Health Estimates 2023 ... 2000-2023', Geneva, WHO, 2026; files dated 2026-09-30), and WHO states 'the 2000-2023 estimates are not comparable to previously-released WHO estimates' and, in the methods paper WHO/HSA/DDA/GHE/2026.2, that 'differences between revision series should not be interpreted as time trends'. The 2021 column of the new regional file is therefore a re-estimate and need not round to the report's 15 000 / 66 000 / 84 000 / 83 000 / 35 000 / 17 000, which come from the GHE 2021 release (report p. 12). A mismatch would not be an error in either source. The GHE 2021 regional summary file is no longer linked on the page; a person should ask WHO (GHE team) or check whether an archived copy exists before comparing. (3) Rounded WHO values seen on 21 Oct 2026, all consistent with the ledger: 2021 (GHE 2021 release) Western Pacific 84 000 / 4.3, South-East Asia 83 000 / 4.0, African 66 000 / 5.6, Eastern Mediterranean 35 000 / 4.4, Americas 17 000 / 1.6, European 15 000 / 1.7 (report p. 14, Fig. 2; EMRO 2025 and WPRO 2024 pages repeat 35 000 and 'over 84,000'). 2019 (GHE 2019 release, a different vintage): African Region 39 000 (about 3.56 per 100 000), South-East Asia 70 000, Western Pacific 74 000 (3.8 per 100 000 per AFRO), recorded as new rows; Americas and Eastern Mediterranean 2019-release values not found; European Region 'over 19 000' (WHO/Europe, July 2021) is filed in the companion bundle who-ghe-europe-9155-check. No value for 2023 was found anywhere in text form. (4) The GHO OData API holds no GHE drowning series (only two alcohol-programme indicators with 2002/2004 country data), and data.who.int has no drowning indicator, so there is no JSON route to these figures. (5) Corrections: who-region-eur carries unfilled placeholders '{SRC}' and '{WHO}' in source and url; proposed values copy the sibling regional rows and were checked against the report and its publication page. Notes on who-ghe-2021 and who-ghe-2019 flag that their URL now serves a different vintage. (6) IHME/GBD was not used.
